The Prophet let Khaibar's Jews work its land for half the fruit as long as he wished; Umar later expelled them, and all Jews and Christians, from Hijaz.
At Bait-ul-Midras the Prophet tells the Jews they will be safe if they embrace Islam, that he wants to expel them, and that they may sell their property.
On his deathbed the Prophet invoked Allah's curse on the Jews and Christians for building places of worship at their prophets' graves, warning Muslims against doing so.
Muslims will follow Jews' and Christians' ways; the adhan and a prayer posture differ from theirs; a parable gives Muslims double wages; Jews are cursed for selling forbidden fat.
The Jews and Christians do not dye their grey hair, so Muslims are told to do the opposite.
The greatest losers of verse 18.103 are said to be the Jews, who disbelieved Muhammad, and the Christians, who denied Paradise's food and drink, not Al-Haruriyya, the pledge-breakers.
When his illness worsened the Prophet, covering his face with a Khamisa, cursed the Jews and Christians for taking their prophets' graves as places of worship, warning his followers.
At Bait al-Midras the Prophet thrice called the Jews to embrace Islam and be safe, then said he wanted to exile them, so those with property could sell it.
